geopolitics_summary: EU climate policy momentum faces headwinds from populist election threats; UK-EU energy deal progressing; Mediterranean geopolitical tensions resurface.

themes.headline: EU backs COP31 electrification target; weak commitment depth evident
themes.why_it_matters: Electrification pledge accelerates power demand outlook; however, low explicit endorsement count signals weak enforcement risk. Affects multi-year power curve vol and EUA carry.

themes.headline: Spain election snap vote threatens EU's loudest climate-policy champion
themes.why_it_matters: Conservative victory would relax climate rules, reducing power decarbonization urgency and EUA demand. Direct risk to EU ETS price and Spanish power policy consistency.

themes.headline: UK-EU electricity interconnector deal nears completion; price convergence risk
themes.why_it_matters: Increased cross-Channel capacity and price convergence could depress continental power prices via arbitrage. Direct DA and Cal+1 curve pressure if UK electricity cheaper than EU.

themes.headline: Turkey-Greece maritime dispute threatens eastern Mediterranean energy corridor
themes.why_it_matters: Mediterranean gas infrastructure dispute could disrupt alternative LNG import routes or gas flow certainty. Indirect TTF risk if supply corridor access limited or regional tensions escalate.

themes.headline: Populist surge threatens to unwind EU climate policy consensus post-COP31
themes.why_it_matters: Election gains by far-right parties signal future ETS weakening and decarbonization delays. Downside risk to long-term EUA valuations and power decarbonization path; multi-year curve pressure.

watchlist: Spain snap election (later November 2026) — conservative climate-policy relaxation risk.
UK-EU electricity deal finalization — interconnector capacity/price arbitrage impact timing.
COP31 follow-up enforcement steps — electrification pledge credibility and EUA trajectory.
Turkey-Greece maritime dispute escalation — eastern Mediterranean gas corridor security.
